content.title: About
content.content: Egg foo yung is a classic Chinese dish consisting of an omelette mixed with vegetables, meat or seafood and fried in oil. In the NFS (1966) version the dish appears as a pixelated Easter egg, but retains its characteristic flavor and aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name comes from Cantonese “egg fu yung”, literally “egg omelette”.
Traditional recipes often include soy sauce, ginger and scallions.
In NFS 1966 the dish is hidden as an Easter egg, unlocked only by performing special tricks.
It is usually served with rice or noodles, but in the game it can only be “eaten” as a visual effect.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Eggs and added meat or seafood make the dish a good source of complete protein.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs provide vitamin B12 and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Vegetables such as broccoli or carrots add antioxidant properties.

items.title: Low in carbs
items.content: With a high protein and low starch content, it fits well into low‑carb diets.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Egg foo yung contains eggs, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce adds a notable amount of salt, which may be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: The dish is often fried in a generous amount of oil, increasing its calorie density.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The dish is typically served hot, cut into bite‑size pieces. In the game it is “consumed” by triggering a special event, after which an eating animation plays.

content.title: Storage
content.content: In reality, cooked egg foo yung should be refrigerated and eaten within 2‑3 days. In the game the object remains in memory until the level is reloaded.
